sentences.text: 2. The 2nd respondent lodged an FIR stating that the Directors of the Co-operative Society induced him to deposit a sum of Rs.1 Crore by promising to pay interest at 12% per annum.
It is further stated that, despite receiving the money, the Directors have neither paid any interest nor returned the deposited amount.
The 2nd respondent, although served with notice, did not choose to appear in person or through counsel; therefore, he is being dealt with ex parte.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent-State were heard.

5. The petitioner has produced a copy of a communication dated 5.8.2020 issued to the President of the Co-operative Society, stating that he had received a sum of Rs.1,04,00,000 (Rupees One Crore and Four Lakhs Only) for procuring the land, of which Rs.1 Crore was returned and the balance of Rs.4 Lakhs was adjusted toward travel and other expenses.
The 2nd respondent has not appeared before this Court to challenge the validity of the communication.
Therefore, it is implied that the amount received by the 2nd respondent was for the procurement of land and not as a deposit.

Moreover, the 2nd respondent has not produced any substantive evidence to establish that the deposit of Rs.1 Crore was intended as a fixed deposit in lieu of the Co-operative Society paying interest at 12% per annum.
In such circumstances, the continuation of the investigation would amount to an abuse of the process of law.
6. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
The impugned FIR in Crime No.42/2024 registered by the Channammanakere Acchu Kattu Police Station, insofar as it relates to the petitioner, is hereby quashed.
